'''Joe Alread''' (Joseph Alread; listed as Joe Atread on the 1998 Worlds packet) finished 3rd at the [[1996 Decipher World Championship]].<ref name="wf">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com:80/wf00p2.htm World Championships 2000 / history of the world finals] (Wayback)</ref> He also won the [[1997 GenCon Open]],<ref name="dec97q" /> [[DecipherCon 1999 Iron Man]],<ref name="dc99sw11_1" /> and the [[2000 Origins Open]].<ref name="dc00fin" /> He was [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]] Gold 79 from Normal, Illinois,<ref name="decsq-prof">[http://www.decipher.com/volunteers/squadrons/players/alreadjoe.html Star Wars CCG Squadrons: Gold 79 profile], decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000618225505/http://decipher.com:80/volunteers/squadrons/players/alreadjoe.html Internet Archive]</ref> and a Decipher SWCCG design guest on [[Radio Free Decipher]].<ref name="rfd">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Radio_Free_Decipher Radio Free Decipher episode index], LOTR-TCG PC wiki</ref>

[[Chuck Kallenbach]] wrote that Alread was among testers who flagged [[Operatives]] before the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]].<ref name="ck-worst">[https://iquotemyself.wordpress.com/2007/02/28/it-was-the-worst-of-times-period/ It was the Worst of Times. Period.], Chuck Kallenbach, i quote myself (28 February 2007). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20210719164120/https://iquotemyself.wordpress.com/2007/02/28/it-was-the-worst-of-times-period/ Internet Archive].</ref> His Decipher profile was one line: "The details of my life are quite inconsequential really..."<ref name="decsq-prof" />
